info.title: CaseForge Verifier
info.description:
Verifier compares a submitted final draft against its original Vault record and
answers `PASS` or `BLOCK`. It never trusts source facts supplied in the request: the
record is always read from `GET {VAULT_URL}/engagements/{record_id}`.

`BLOCK` is a normal result and is returned with HTTP 200 and a populated `problems`
list. An HTTP error is not a verdict and can never authorise publication.

Deterministic checks (quantities, naming consent, citation references) can BLOCK on
their own, but they cannot produce a PASS. Every PASS additionally requires the
independent semantic gate to assess every visible span against the source, so
`OPENAI_API_KEY` must be configured for any PASS in any language.

`GET /health` reports liveness only and contacts no dependency. See
`docs/CF-123-runbook.md` for setup, dependencies, timeouts and troubleshooting.

post.summary: Verify a draft against its Vault record
post.description:
Reads the source record from Vault, normalises the submitted draft, runs the deterministic checks and, only if those find nothing, the independent semantic gate.

`language` defaults to `en`. Deterministic checks can BLOCK without any model call, but a PASS always requires the semantic assessment, so the provider must be configured.

A PASS is not permission to publish: Publisher verifies the final display content again through this same route.

200.description: A completed verification. `BLOCK` is a normal result: it is reported here with HTTP 200 and a populated `problems` list, never as an HTTP error.

post.summary: Verify a draft supplied with its record body
post.description:
Takes `{record, mcs}`. The submitted `record` is used only to confirm that its `id` matches the path; **every fact still comes from Vault**, so editing the submitted record cannot change the verdict.

Deprecated. Use `POST /verify` with `{record_id, draft, language}`.

VerificationReport.description: The verification result. `problems` is empty on PASS and populated on BLOCK; different checks report different fields, so only `type` and `why` are common.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: One reason a draft was blocked. Different checks report different fields, so only `type` and `why` are always present.

type.description: The check that produced the problem.

why.description: Why the draft cannot be published.

span.description: JSON pointer into the draft, e.g. `/sections/outcomes/0/outcomes`. Absent on problems that are not scoped to one span.

value.description: The offending value. Usually a string; some claim checks report a list.

DraftInput.title: DraftInput
DraftInput.description:
The draft to verify. Two shapes are accepted and normalised to the same canonical
document before any check runs:

* each section as plain prose, e.g. `"outcomes": "Payment latency reduced by 45%."`
* each section as a list of MCS entries, e.g.
  `"outcomes": [{"outcomes": "...", "page": "eng-cf123-01"}]`

`sections` is the only required key, and at least one section must contain text. Use
`title` or `titles`, never both. `titles`, `citations` and `client_named` are filled
in by normalisation when absent, so they are not required on input.

Every source identity in the draft must agree with the request `record_id`:
`engagement_id`, `engagement_ids`, each entry's `page` and each citation's `page_ref`.
A `language` key, if present, must equal the request `language`. These cross-field
rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema alone; a conflict returns 422.

engagement_id.description: If present, must equal the request `record_id`.

sections.description: The standard case-study sections. Absent sections normalise to an empty list, but at least one must contain text.

context.description: Client type and region, composed from the source record.

technology.description: Technologies recorded on the source, joined into one entry.

outcomes.description: Measured outcomes, or a `[MISSING: ...]` marker when the source records none.

client_named.description: Defaults to false. Setting it true when the source record does not set `may_be_named` does not grant consent; the naming checks still compare against the record.

language.description: If present, must equal the request `language`.

BearerAuth.description: Optional service-to-service credential. This API never enforces a bearer token on its own endpoints. An incoming `Authorization` header is forwarded to Vault unchanged; when it is absent the configured `CASEFORGE_TOKEN` is sent instead. A rejected credential therefore surfaces as Vault's own 401 or 403, not as a local authentication failure.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-ID
CorrelationId.description: Trace forwarded to every dependency and returned on handled responses. Any printable-ASCII value of at most 4096 characters is accepted; it does not have to be a UUID. Omit it to have one generated.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Validated under the same printable-ASCII and 4096-character rule as the other shared headers. This API neither deduplicates on it nor forwards it to Vault, so sending it guarantees no persistent deduplication.

BadHeader.description: A shared HTTP header was rejected before the route ran; the response still carries a generated trace. The limit is 4096 characters of printable ASCII (code points 32-126) on `X-Correlation-ID`, `Authorization` and `Idempotency-Key`.
